title: Hazlewood Edges Out Boland for Australia First Test as Selectors Eye 21-Match Season
excerpt: George Bailey concedes Scott Boland is building a case to be one of Australia’s big three quicks, but Josh Hazlewood gets the nod for Darwin despite injury concerns.
body:
• Josh Hazlewood has been selected over Scott Boland in Australia's pace attack for the first Test against Bangladesh in Darwin, despite Boland's consistent Ashes performances and superior availability record.
  • Chair of selectors George Bailey acknowledged Boland is "mounting a strong case" to be considered one of Australia's "big three" quicks alongside Pat Cummins and Mitchell Starc.
  • Hazlewood's fitness remains a concern — he missed the entire Ashes and has been injured in the first match of four of his last five home summers.
  • The selection comes as India prepares for its own two-Test series in Sri Lanka beginning August 15, with both nations jockeying for position in the World Test Championship standings.

Josh Hazlewood has won the selection battle against Scott Boland for Australia's first Test against Bangladesh in Darwin, but the debate over the veteran quick's place in the pecking order is far from settled. Chair of selectors George Bailey conceded that Boland is building a compelling case to break into Australia's frontline pace trio, setting up what could be an extended rotation across a punishing 21-Test schedule over the next 12 months.

The decision reunites Pat Cummins, Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc as Australia's starting pace unit for the first time since the Caribbean tour against the West Indies last year, with Nathan Lyon returning as the lone spinner after missing three Ashes Tests with a serious hamstring injury.

Boland's Record Demands Respect

Boland's numbers make the omission difficult to justify on merit alone. The 37-year-old has taken 82 wickets at 18.58 from 19 Tests, with 69 of those coming on home soil at an average of just 16.20. He played all five Ashes Tests while Hazlewood sat out the entire series through injury, and he has never missed a Test through fitness concerns since his debut in December 2021.

"I know Scotty would never say it, but I think he's mounting a strong case that when you use the words 'the big three,' he could be one of those," Bailey told reporters. "We won't be locking in an XI this far out, but we do know that across this two-Test series, the depth is there."

"I think he's mounting a strong case that when you use the words 'the big three,' he could be one of those."

— George Bailey, Australia's chair of selectors, on Scott Boland

Managing Hazlewood's Workload

Hazlewood's selection comes with an asterisk. The 35-year-old has 295 wickets at 24.21 from 76 Tests but has sustained injuries in the first Test or first-class match of four of his last five Australian summers. Cricket Australia's high-performance staff have adjusted his training and physical preparation over the past two months to reduce the risk of a breakdown.

"There has been some adjustments to both his training and some of his physical prep to try and alleviate some of those setbacks that he's had," Bailey said. The selectors rested Hazlewood, Starc and Cummins from white-ball tours of Pakistan and Bangladesh in June to give them a training block similar to what Boland undertakes every winter as a Test-only bowler.

The approach contrasts with last winter, when Hazlewood chose to keep playing white-ball cricket after the Caribbean tour. He subsequently suffered hamstring and Achilles injuries that ruled him out of the entire Ashes summer.

WTC Stakes for India and Australia

Australia's selection dynamics carry implications beyond the Bangladesh series. India begins its own two-Test series in Sri Lanka on August 15 in Galle, captained by Shubman Gill, with Jasprit Bumrah returning to the squad. Both nations are positioned in the middle of the World Test Championship standings, with Australia needing wins to stay in contention for the 2027 final.

Bailey indicated that the selectors are not pre-planning rest periods for any of their quicks, but acknowledged that across 21 Tests — including a potential home series against India in January and February — "there will be different times when there will be different names and a different line-up." Michael Neser, who took 5-42 in the second Ashes Test, was also left out of the 13-man squad despite his standout performance, underscoring the depth of Australia's pace stocks.

For Indian fans tracking Australia's bowling firepower, the key question is whether Hazlewood can stay fit through a long summer — and whether Boland's irresistible home record will eventually force the selectors' hand before the next Border-Gavaskar Trophy.
